title: U-Net & Segmentation
interviewAnswer: U-Net combines an encoder that captures context with a decoder that restores spatial resolution, using skip connections to preserve fine localization information.
why: U-Net is a standard encoder–decoder architecture for segmentation and reconstruction where both context and precise spatial localization matter.
intuition: The encoder compresses spatial information while learning context; the decoder restores resolution. Skip connections copy high-resolution features from matching encoder stages to recover detail.
deepDive: Downsampling increases semantic context but loses exact position. U-Net concatenates or combines encoder features with decoder features at corresponding scales. Output heads depend on task: class logits per pixel/voxel for segmentation, image channels for reconstruction. 3D U-Nets extend convolutions to volumes but consume much more memory.
workedExample: In pore segmentation, deep features identify material context while shallow skip features preserve exact boundary locations that would be blurred by the bottleneck alone.
commonMistakes: Calling U-Net skip connections residual additions by default; classic U-Net concatenates.
Ignoring output activation/loss for multi-class vs binary segmentation.
Using huge 3D volumes without patch/memory planning.
production: Tiled inference needs overlap/blending to avoid seams. Monitor resolution/preprocessing and memory use carefully for 3D deployment.
